Information Processing22Information processing converts raw data into meaningful information. There are seven stages of information processing: 1.3
Data collection23Data can be collected by various methods like observation, experiments, interviews, surveys, etc. The data collection method depends on the scope and the data type.A
Organisation24Organisation means managing, categorising and classifying the collected data in a specific way, examples include:B Data arrangementData validationData type conversion
Storage25After organisation, Data can be stored as physical copies or in a digital storage.Common digital storages include:CHard diskUSB flash drive
Processing26Processing means editing, modifying and updating data. The can be categorized as:Text processingImage processingAudio processingVideo processingD

Analysis27Data analysis extracts meaningful information from the processed data. For example:Putting the annual average temperature of Hong Kong in the past 50 years into a spreadsheet to identify the climate trends E

Transmission28Data transmission involves transmitters, media and receivers.Network is one of the possible media. It requires that both the transmitter and the receiver use the same protocol for communication.F
Presentation29Presentation means the output of data or information through various media. Common examples include:GTextImageVideoAudio

Information Age32What will happen to your life without computers?1.4

Definition33With the rapid development of information and communication technology, microcomputers, internet and search engines have been improved constantly.Accessing and publishing information have become easier and more popular:ASearch engineSocial mediaStreaming platform

Causes34The causes of the information age include:BPersonal computers and mobile devicesApplication designCommunication networkPersonal computers and mobile devices have become more widespread as they are more affordable. The computing power of mobile devices has increased over the years, which allows users to process and transmit data anytime and anywhere.Interactive design of software allows people to access desired information directly.The invention of optical fibres and the advancement of telecommunication technology have enhanced the mobility and the coverage of information.

Development35The developments of information and communication technology include:CInternet of ThingsBig DataArtificial intelligenceNetwork of physical objectsThe vast amount of data gathers due to the high usage of digital devices and online platformsHas the power to process and analyse a large amount of data in a short time.

Information Literacy36We should consider information literacy from different aspects before accepting and using information. DIntellectual propertyIt is unethical and illegal to use or gain benefits from others’ intellectual properties without their permission.Data privacyWhen sharing information, we should respect others’ privacy.CredibilityWe should consider the authoritativeness, validity and relevance of the information.Extraction and organisationWe should search information from various media, then extract and organise our findings.
Purpose4Information systems are implemented to:Automate processesReduce human errorsImprove efficiencyA
Data5Data is stored in computer storage devices, it can be used by programs for input or output.Examples of data include:Medical history of a patientWeather dataB
